Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The Zimbabwe players are out in the middle. Jan Frylinck and Malan Kruger to open for Namibia. Wellington Masakadza to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

Namibia will think about where they went wrong! Maybe they didn't read the conditions before the toss but despite opting to bowl first, they never stemmed the run flow and chased the game throughout the innings. Almost every bowler went above 10 runs per over, which just tells how much they struggled to build the pressure. Right then, Namibia have a mountain to climb. It's a belter of a pitch to bat on. Namibia need to apply themselves and a good start is a must. Can they chase it down? Stay tuned to find out.

A fantastic knock from Zimbabwe and they have successfully breached the 200-mark. Zimbabwe have one man to thank, the 21-year-old Brian Bennett was at his best today, eyeing his maiden T20I century but fell just 6 runs short. Brian Bennett and Tadiwanashe Marumani went berserk at the top, unjustifying Namibia's decision to bowl first. Zimbabwe hammered them all over the park right from the word go and locked in the target of around 200 very early on in the innings. Tadiwanashe Marumani was the aggressor initially but once he fell after his fifty, Brian Bennett picked up the baton and changed gears. Ryan Burl, too, played a fine cameo of 22 off 9 deliveries, locking in for the big target. The skipper, Sikandar Raza, joined in at the fag end of the innings to put the icing on the cake.
Sikandar Raza does what he always does. Once again, delivers a perfect cameo of 23 runs off just 11 deliveries to wrap up the Zimbabwe innings.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the national anthems and we are all set to get going. Gerhard Erasmus and Co. disperse from the huddle and take their respective positions on the field. Brian Bennett and Tadiwanashe Marumani are the two openers for Zimbabwe. JJ Smit will start the attack for Namibia. Smit to Bennett. Away we go...
We are moments away from the first ball, but before that, the two teams will line up for the national anthems. It will be Namibia's national anthem first, followed by that of Zimbabwe.

Namibia (Playing XI) - Jan Frylinck, Malan Kruger, Jan Nicol Loftie-Eaton, Gerhard Erasmus (C), JJ Smit, Dylan Leicher, Zane Green (WK), Ruben Trumpelmann, Bernard Scholtz, Jack Brassell, Alexander Volschenk.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Tadiwanashe Marumani (WK), Brendan Taylor, Dion Myers, Sikandar Raza (C), Ryan Burl, Tashinga Musekiwa, Wellington Masakadza, Brad Evans, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani.
TOSS - Namibia have won the toss and will BOWL first.

The hosts, Zimbabwe, are the favourites as we head into this series. They have been playing against quite a few big teams, which have helped them grow from strength-to-strength. Zimbabwe recently played against Sri Lanka and despite losing the series 1-2, they put in a tough fight against the Asian side in the home series. Zimbabwe will hope to bounce back against Namibia, who are four places below them in the ICC T20I rankings. Namibia, in comparison to Zimbabwe, have played fewer matches of cricket against big sides but arrive into this series with momentum, having just completed a 3-0 series sweep over Canada. Both teams have a balanced squad but Zimbabwe have an edge due to the favourable home ground conditions. Who do you think will win? Toss and team sheets next.

Hello everyone, to the first of the three-match T20I series between Zimbabwe and Namibia. Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo is all set to host all three T20Is between two quality sides who are looking to build up their squad for the upcoming ICC Men’s T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier 2025. Who are you backing?
...MATCH DAY...

The countdown to the World T20 Qualifiers begins right here as Zimbabwe and Namibia lock horns in the first of a three-match T20I series, promising a fierce battle between two evenly matched sides and serving as a good warm up before the crunch games. Zimbabwe may have lost their last T20I series 2-1 to Sri Lanka, but they pushed the Asian side to the brink and showed they can go toe-to-toe with stronger teams. Sikandar Raza remains their talisman with both bat and ball, supported by the consistency of Brian Bennett and Sean Williams, while their pace department is packed with quality led by the pair of Richard Ngarava and Blessing Muzarabani. However, death bowling woes and fielding lapses are areas they must tighten up to avoid slipping in crucial moments. Namibia arrive with confidence after a convincing 3-0 win over Canada in their last T20I series and will lean on skipper Gerhard Erasmus and Jan Nicol Loftie-Eaton to anchor the batting. Their bowling boasts variety and discipline with the likes of Ruben Trumpelmann and Ben Shikongo, but middle-order fragility and inexperience in high-pressure situations remain concerns. With both sides using this series as a key tune-up ahead of the qualifiers, expect a fiery opener where every run and wicket will count, and momentum could swing sharply in either direction.
